history.sg_progress: The Administration is looking forward to the outcome of the resident coordinator system review, which will inform the way forward on strategy and action to be taken to strengthen resource mobilization for a smooth inflow of resources and an optimum functioning of the resident coordinator system. The review has been launched, and the relevant report of the Secretary-General (A/75/905), which contains proposals for options for the way forward on funding the resident coordinator system, was issued on 7 June 2021. The suggested options are to: (a) fund the resident coordinator system completely with assessed contributions; or (b) fund the resident coordinator system through a hybrid model, in which the existing agency cost-sharing arrangement and the 1 per cent coordination levy will remain as is, but the voluntary contributions will be replaced by assessed contributions. The outcome and decision of the General Assembly will determine the way forward on resource mobilization.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its efforts in resource mobilization to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: In its resolution 76/4, the General Assembly decided to retain the hybrid structure of funding for the resident coordinator system and committed to providing sufficient funding for the resident coordinator system on an annual basis starting from 1 January 2022. The Development Coordination Office is currently in discussions with the Executive Office of the Secretary- General on a resource mobilization strategy for 2022 and beyond, with the goal of increasing the number of Member States providing voluntary contributions, the volume of annual contributions from key donors and the number of donors providing multi-year commitments. Development Coordination Office is also carrying out an analysis of the 1 per cent coordination levy generated in 2019–2021 to identify possible gaps in implementation so that they may be actively addressed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Development Coordination Office is making efforts to mobilize resources and close the gap towards a target of $2.81 million per annum, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its resource mobilization efforts to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office has intensified its resource mobilization efforts to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the smooth operation of the resident coordinator system. This, among other efforts, has included meetings of Member States and briefings by United Nations senior leadership and the Development Coordination Office management at the permanent representative and deputy permanent representative level; a round table with permanent representatives and the Secretary-General; resource mobilization letters from Development Coordination Office management; and daily outreach at the technical level. Donor trips at the Assistant Secretary-General level have been envisaged. In addition, efforts include strategic outreach towards the members of the Group of 77 and the Gulf Cooperation Council to broker buy-in and a token contribution to send a signal to their broader constituency. Efforts also include the drafting of five case studies showcasing the partnership between the resident coordinator system and host Governments in a variety of contexts to highlight the added value of the resident coordinator system and help donors make the case to their capitals to fund the system. Through the round table co-convened by Kenya and the United States, the membership has been apprised of the urgency of the funding situation, particularly regarding the need to quickly secure financial predictability and sustainability. The round table succeeded in strengthening momentum with the membership, in follow-up to which several donors have fast-tracked the payment of their 2023 contributions, including Sweden ($5 million), Ireland ($1.5 million), the Kingdom of the Netherlands ($4 million) and Germany ($6.4 million).
history.board_assessment: Given that the Development Coordination Office has intensified its resource mobilization efforts to close the gap towards the target of $2.81 million a year, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its resource mobilization efforts to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office consistently followed up with permanent missions through resource mobilization letters and engaged with them at the technical level. As a result, in 2023 the donor base increased to 29, which is 2 more than in 2022. Kenya was onboarded as a new, forty-sixth donor to the Special Purpose Trust Fund. The Development Coordination Office is reaching out to potential new donors to solicit their contributions and expand the donor base for the Special Purpose Trust Fund in 2024. As at 3 April 2024, 16 donors have made contributions or firm or soft commitments, including Group of 77 donors. Resource mobilization for the resident coordinator system has been a priority for the Assistant Secretary- General of the Development Coordination Office, in particular, and an effort requiring colleagues across various Development Coordination Office teams to step in to support this undertaking in addition to their responsibilities to make the case for the coordination function with the aim of mobilizing sufficient voluntary contributions. In addition, the Secretary- General conducted the transparent and inclusive, informal consultations with Member States during the fourth quarter of 2023, pursuant to the solid Economic and Social Council resolution 2023/31 of 26 July 2023 regarding the persistent shortfall of the resident coordinator system. In that connection, the Secretary- General has now submitted a report on the revised estimates to the Fifth Committee of the General Assembly. Since the recommendation was to intensify the Administration’s efforts in resource mobilization and the Administration has left no stone unturned to ensure sustainable funding support for the resident coordinator system, the Board is still requested to consider closing this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the resources mobilized in 2023 were still far below the target of $281 million per annum for adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its resource mobilization efforts to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: Since March 2025, the Development Coordination Office has continued to conduct full-fledged outreach and resource mobilization, engaging at all levels and working with senior management and across teams, including the United Nations team in Brussels and the United Nations team in Washington, D.C. In order to address the chronic underfunding of the resident coordinator system, the Secretary- General, in his relevant report to the General Assembly (A/78/753), proposed to replace the volatile and unpredictable voluntary contribution funding stream with more predictable and sustainable funding for core activities of the system. The Office supported the Secretary-General and the Deputy Secretary-General in engaging with Member States on this proposal throughout 2024, which led to the adoption of Assembly resolution 79/258, in which the Assembly decided to provide a commitment authority not exceeding $53 million for the period from 1 January to 31 December 2025. In addition, the Office continued its daily engagement with the technical focal points in missions and capitals in order to make the case for investment in the resident coordinator system. Moreover, the Assistant Secretary- General for Development Coordination held meetings with the Assistant Secretaries-General of United Nations Sustainable Development Group members to drive forward collective efforts for an increase in quality funding. Similarly, the Office continued to follow up to ensure that the members of the United Nations Sustainable Development Group transferred their portions of the cost- sharing arrangement in a timely manner, and continued to report on the coordination levy. The Development Coordination Office is also recruiting additional staff on a temporary basis to further intensify outreach, resource mobilization and intergovernmental support.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Development Coordination Office has been intensifying its efforts to mobilize resources in order to reach the annual target of $2.81 million, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 509 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration intensify its resource mobilization efforts to ensure adequate, predictable and sustainable funding to support the resident coordinator system.
history.reference_raw: Report of the Board for the year ended 31 December 2020 6
history.sg_progress: The Development Coordination Office continues to advance its outreach and resource mobilization efforts, actively engaging with Member States at all levels. These efforts are closely coordinated across the Office, including senior management, and with the United Nations teams in Brussels and Washington, D.C. The Office maintains consistent, daily engagement with technical focal points in missions in New York and in capitals, advocating for voluntary contributions to the resident coordinator system and, where feasible, application of the levy at source. During 2025, the Development Coordination Office leadership has convened a series of meetings with counterparts from capitals on the margins of United Nations events. In parallel, the senior leadership continues to emphasize the importance of enhancing the quality of funding. Strategic opportunities, such as annual ambassador conferences and strategic dialogues, are being leveraged to update Member States on the system’s impact, supported by targeted communication materials and advocacy efforts. Internally, the Office has strengthened its capacity to support the intensification of outreach and resource mobilization activities.
